problems: Booking availability is disclosed only after the main CTA is pressed, while the page invites choosing a time and says We'll call you before a tool has been selected.
The phone demo stacks a schedule, waitlist and tall text area before its small playback dots; controls and the made-up-example disclosure arrive much later than the initial appointment rows.
The lower page's large alternating colour bands and extended HIPAA explanation make a relatively simple service feel longer to scan than necessary, especially on a phone.

reason: B has the stronger desktop composition, more coherent colour and type hierarchy, and an explicit, dismissible response when booking is unavailable. A has the more legible manual timeline and better-sized phone stage controls; simplifying B's tall phone artifact and disclosing booking status beside the CTA would make the preference firmer.
